headline: Last session: Sensex crashes over 1,400 points as banking stocks trigger sharp market sell-off

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Wednesday, 25 November.

why: Profit-taking by investors following a continuous four-week market rally.
Heavy selling pressure concentrated in banking and financial stocks.
Widespread drop across sectors, including metal stocks.
Sharp reversal after early session morning gains failed to hold.
whatHappening: Indian stock markets are closed on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
On the last trading day (23 November), Sensex shed over 1,400 points while Nifty dropped below 25,400.
Investor wealth reduced by over Rs 5.6 lakh crore during Monday's session.
SEBI urged market intermediaries to stop publishing IPO Grey Market Premium (GMP).
summary: Indian markets are closed today for the Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday. In the last session on 23 November, benchmark indices suffered a sharp decline with Sensex dropping over 1,400 points led by heavy profit-taking in banking stocks. Trading will resume on Wednesday, 25 November.
